headline: Structure-informed models prioritize zinc-binding and multi-target ligands
label: Structure Guided Ligand Prioritization
summary: Recent work pairs consensus ML and pharmacophore models with SMARTS libraries and fused target embeddings for ligand prioritization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of small molecules from target-centric features rather than from experimental screening alone. Two published items apply substructure- or pharmacophore-driven models: a 41-pattern SMARTS library of zinc binding groups, derived from classifiers and substructure analysis, for Zn-metalloenzyme inhibitor discovery, and a consensus machine learning and pharmacophore approach predicting BSEP inhibitors linked to liver injury, validated against 11 in vitro-tested compounds. The third item, a multi-target drug design method, instead fuses target protein sequence embeddings into individual and similarity latent vectors to generate ligands. What is new is the use of target-derived sequence representations for multi-target generation, alongside rule-based and consensus classifiers that encode chemotype and pharmacophore knowledge. The set is heterogeneous, and only the BSEP item reports experimental checks in its summary.
